accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='combobox' to the search input with aria-expanded reflecting open/closed state
Apply role='listbox' to the results container and role='option' to each result item
Use aria-activedescendant on the input pointing to the currently highlighted option ID
Auto-focus the search input immediately on palette mount
Navigate results with ArrowUp / ArrowDown; wrap at list boundaries
Activate the selected option on Enter key press
Close the palette on Escape key press and restore focus to the trigger
Announce result count changes using aria-live='polite' on a status element
Group results under role='group' with aria-label describing the group category
accessibilityRationale: Combobox role communicates to assistive technology that the input controls a list of options
Listbox and option roles allow screen readers to announce each result and total count
aria-activedescendant allows screen readers to track the highlighted option without moving DOM focus
Auto-focusing removes a click barrier for keyboard users who triggered the palette via shortcut
Arrow key navigation is the expected interaction pattern for list traversal
Enter activation matches the standard selection behaviour keyboard users expect in any picker
Escape provides a safe, predictable exit that restores the user's previous context
Live region announcements ensure screen reader users know when results filter dynamically
Result grouping with labels helps screen reader users understand the category structure at a glance
responsiveGridPresets: Centered floating console card overlay with absolute viewport boundaries.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' to the modal container element
Add aria-labelledby pointing to the modal's visible heading element
Add aria-describedby pointing to the modal's body description if present
Trap keyboard Tab and Shift+Tab focus within the open modal
Move focus to the first interactive element on open
Restore focus to the trigger element that opened the modal on close
Close the modal on Escape key press
Provide a visible close button with aria-label='Close dialog'
accessibilityRationale: Screen readers must announce the dialog boundary so users know they've entered a modal context
Labelling the modal gives screen reader users an immediate understanding of its purpose
Describing the body prevents users from navigating before understanding the content
Focus trapping prevents keyboard users from interacting with background content while the dialog is open
Moving focus on open ensures screen reader users start at the right context
Restoring focus on close returns the user to their last position — critical for keyboard-only users
Escape is the universally expected dismissal shortcut that keyboard users rely on
An accessible close button ensures the action is discoverable without a mouse
responsiveGridPresets: Responsive modal centered on small screens, scaling up to max-w-lg on desktop.

accessibilityRequirements: Use semantic heading hierarchy inside each card (h2 for plan name, h3 for price)
Ensure CTA buttons have descriptive text: 'Get Started with Pro' not just 'Get Started'
Apply aria-describedby on each CTA button pointing to its feature list
Ensure colour contrast of 4.5:1 minimum on all pricing text and CTA buttons
Mark the recommended plan with aria-label='Recommended plan: Pro'
accessibilityRationale: Heading hierarchy allows screen reader users to navigate between plans using heading shortcuts
Descriptive button text prevents screen reader users from encountering ambiguous 'Get Started' labels repeated three times
aria-describedby links the CTA to its features so users understand what they are purchasing
Colour contrast ensures readability for users with low vision or colour blindness
The recommended plan must be announced to screen reader users who cannot see the visual highlight
responsiveGridPresets: Single column on mobile, three-column pricing matrix on tablet and desktop.

accessibilityRequirements: Wrap in <nav> with aria-label='Main navigation' or 'Side navigation'
Apply aria-current='page' on the active route link
Apply aria-expanded on the toggle button controlling the sidebar
When in overlay mode (mobile), trap focus inside and close on Escape
Provide visually hidden screen reader text indicating collapsed/expanded state
Ensure all nav links have descriptive text — no 'Click here' labels
accessibilityRationale: Named nav landmark allows screen reader users to jump directly to navigation
aria-current='page' communicates the user's current location to assistive technology
aria-expanded tells screen reader users whether the sidebar is open or collapsed
Focus trapping in overlay mode prevents keyboard users from reaching obscured background content
Hidden state descriptions ensure screen reader users understand the sidebar's current visibility state
Descriptive link text allows users browsing link lists to understand destinations out of context
responsiveGridPresets: Sticky panel on desktop, collapsing to a bottom or slide-out menu on mobile.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='tablist' to the tab container element
Apply role='tab' and aria-selected='true'/'false' to each tab button
Apply role='tabpanel' to each panel and link it to its tab via aria-labelledby
Apply aria-controls on each tab pointing to its associated panel ID
Navigate between tabs with ArrowLeft / ArrowRight; Tab moves focus into the active panel
Ensure inactive panels are hidden with the hidden attribute — not only visually
accessibilityRationale: tablist groups the tab buttons so screen readers announce the set as a navigation region
aria-selected communicates which tab is active without relying on visual-only cues
tabpanel with aria-labelledby ensures users know which tab's content they are reading
aria-controls makes the tab-panel relationship machine-readable for assistive technology
Arrow key navigation is the ARIA design pattern — Tab is reserved for moving into panel content
Properly hidden panels prevent screen readers from reading inactive content during navigation
responsiveGridPresets: Horizontal tab bar on desktop, converting to vertical stack or select input on mobile.

accessibilityRequirements: Use aria-label='Step X of Y: Step Name' on each step indicator
Apply aria-current='step' on the active step indicator
Move focus to the heading or first input of each new step after navigation
Announce step transitions with aria-live='polite'
Provide a text-based step count (e.g. 'Step 2 of 4') not only icon-based
Ensure Back and Next buttons have descriptive aria-labels
accessibilityRationale: Step position announcement prevents screen reader users from losing orientation in a multi-step flow
aria-current='step' communicates progress state beyond visual progress bars
Moving focus on step change ensures users are immediately aware of the new step
Live region announcements prevent confusion after a step transition completes
Text-based step count is readable by screen readers that may not interpret SVG icon sequences
Descriptive button labels give keyboard users confidence about the consequence of Next
responsiveGridPresets: Centered wizard card with a full-width progress indicator above the form.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='log' or aria-live='polite' to the stream container
Each activity item should have a visible timestamp accessible to screen readers
Use <time datetime='ISO-8601-date'> for machine-readable timestamps
Ensure new items appended to the log are announced by the live region
accessibilityRationale: role='log' informs assistive technology that this is an auto-updating feed of events
Visible timestamps provide sighted and screen reader users with chronological context
machine-readable datetime attributes allow browsers and AT to format dates per user locale
Live region announcements ensure real-time activity is communicated to screen reader users
responsiveGridPresets: Single-column vertical cards stack with infinite scroll or pagination.

accessibilityRequirements: Pair each numeric metric with a visible text label — never use the number alone
Use aria-label on the card to provide a full summary: 'Monthly Revenue: $12,400, up 8% from last month'
Ensure colour-coded trend indicators (green up, red down) also have text labels
Apply sufficient colour contrast on metric values (4.5:1 minimum)
accessibilityRationale: Numbers without labels are meaningless to screen reader users who lack visual layout context
Full aria-label summaries allow screen reader users to understand a KPI card in a single announcement
Colour-only trend indicators are invisible to users with colour blindness — text labels are required
Contrast ensures metric values are readable in varying display environments
responsiveGridPresets: Auto-scaling grid cells, single column on mobile, 2–4 columns on desktop.

accessibilityRequirements: Provide a text summary of the chart's key insight above or below the visualisation
Add role='img' and a descriptive aria-label on the chart container
Provide a data table alternative (role='table') alongside or in a togglable view
Ensure interactive chart elements (hover states, drill-downs) are keyboard operable
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling chart entry animations when requested
accessibilityRationale: Chart SVG/Canvas elements are invisible to screen readers without explicit text alternatives
role='img' with aria-label provides at minimum a summary for users who cannot access the visual
A data table alternative gives screen reader users the same data in an accessible format
Keyboard operability ensures power users and motor-impaired users can interact with chart data
Reduced-motion compliance prevents animation-triggered discomfort for vestibular disorder sufferers
responsiveGridPresets: Sizable grid item slot with a minimum height of 200px; responsive width.

accessibilityRequirements: Pause the marquee animation when prefers-reduced-motion is set
Pause animation on hover AND on keyboard focus
Mark the ticker container with aria-hidden='true' if it contains purely decorative content
If ticker contains meaningful logos or names, use aria-label on each item
accessibilityRationale: Continuously moving content triggers vestibular disorders and violates WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide
Hover and focus pausing ensures keyboard users can read ticker content that would otherwise scroll past
aria-hidden on decorative tickers prevents screen readers from announcing repetitive logo names
Meaningful ticker items need labels so screen reader users understand the brands or content being displayed
responsiveGridPresets: Full-width horizontal banner with overflow hidden and CSS marquee animation.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='button' and aria-haspopup='listbox' to the trigger element
Apply aria-expanded='true'/'false' on the trigger
Apply role='listbox' to the options container; role='option' to each item
Navigate options with ArrowUp / ArrowDown; Home to first, End to last
Select with Enter or Space; close with Escape
Close when focus moves outside the dropdown
Use aria-selected='true' on the currently selected option
accessibilityRationale: aria-haspopup signals to screen readers that activating this control opens a list
aria-expanded provides state feedback so screen reader users know the list is open
Listbox and option semantics allow screen readers to announce options and the total count
Arrow key navigation is the standard for list traversal — mouse users have no equivalent constraint
Enter/Space and Escape are the universal selection and dismissal keys
Closing on blur prevents the dropdown from staying open when the user moves on
aria-selected communicates the current value without relying on visual styling
responsiveGridPresets: Inline trigger with an absolutely positioned options list; full-width on mobile.

accessibilityRequirements: Associate every input with a visible <label> using for/id pairing — do not use placeholder as a label substitute
Add aria-required='true' on required fields with a visible asterisk and legend
Add aria-invalid='true' and aria-describedby pointing to the error message on validation failure
Render error messages in a persistent visible element adjacent to the invalid field
Add aria-live='assertive' on an error summary region
Ensure Tab order follows visual reading order
Move focus to the error summary or first invalid field on failed submit
Support Enter key submission from single-line text inputs
accessibilityRationale: Placeholders disappear on input and are not reliably announced by all screen readers
aria-required communicates mandatory fields beyond colour or asterisk alone
aria-invalid with aria-describedby associates the error message directly to its field
Persistent visible errors allow users to review all issues before re-submitting
aria-live='assertive' immediately announces errors to screen reader users
Logical Tab order prevents disorientation on complex forms
Moving focus to errors guides keyboard and screen reader users directly to the problem
Enter-to-submit is the expected keyboard behaviour for standard text inputs
responsiveGridPresets: Single-column stacked labels and inputs, grouping related fields with fieldset/legend.

accessibilityRequirements: Add a <caption> element describing the table's purpose
Use <th> with scope='col' for column headers and scope='row' for row headers
Apply aria-sort='ascending'/'descending'/'none' on sortable column headers
Ensure horizontal scrollability on mobile while maintaining header associations
If rows are interactive (selectable), add role='grid' and manage ArrowKey cell navigation
Provide a text description alongside any chart embedded in the table
accessibilityRationale: A caption gives screen reader users immediate context before they enter the table
scope attributes create explicit associations between data cells and their headers
aria-sort communicates column ordering without reading the full data set
Horizontal scroll preserves data integrity — truncating columns breaks header associations
role='grid' with arrow key navigation allows traversal without losing position
Charts without textual alternatives are completely inaccessible to screen reader users
responsiveGridPresets: Horizontally scrollable on mobile with sticky first column for row context.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply aria-expanded='true'/'false' to each accordion trigger button
Apply aria-controls on the trigger pointing to the panel ID
Apply role='region' and aria-labelledby on each panel
Toggle expand/collapse with Enter or Space; do not intercept Tab
Animate using max-height or clip-path respecting prefers-reduced-motion
Ensure collapsed panel content is not focusable by keyboard
accessibilityRationale: aria-expanded state change is announced to screen readers when a panel opens
aria-controls creates the programmatic link between trigger and panel
role='region' with a label marks each panel as a navigable landmark
Enter/Space are standard toggle keys — Tab must remain free for navigation
Respecting prefers-reduced-motion prevents discomfort for vestibular disorder sufferers
Hidden panel content must be unreachable to prevent keyboard navigation confusion
responsiveGridPresets: Full-width stacked panels with a 1px border separator between items.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='status' and aria-live='polite' for non-critical notifications
Apply role='alert' and aria-live='assertive' for error notifications
Do not move keyboard focus to the toast
Provide a dismiss button with aria-label on persistent toasts
Ensure sufficient colour contrast on toast text (4.5:1 minimum)
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by removing slide/bounce animations
accessibilityRationale: aria-live='polite' queues the announcement after the current screen reader utterance
aria-live='assertive' interrupts immediately — appropriate only for errors requiring urgent attention
Moving focus to a toast disrupts the user's current interaction flow
A dismiss button allows keyboard users to clear persistent toasts without a mouse
Contrast ensures toast messages are readable by users with low vision
Reduced-motion compliance prevents vestibular disorder triggers
responsiveGridPresets: Fixed positioned bottom-right stack, collapsing to bottom-center on mobile.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='combobox' to the text input with aria-autocomplete='list'
Apply aria-expanded reflecting whether the suggestion list is visible
Apply aria-controls pointing to the suggestion listbox element ID
Apply aria-activedescendant on the input tracking the highlighted suggestion ID
Navigate suggestions with ArrowUp / ArrowDown; commit with Enter
Clear input and close suggestions with Escape
Announce suggestion count with aria-live='polite': 'X results available'
Allow users to type freely without forcing a suggestion selection
accessibilityRationale: aria-autocomplete='list' signals that suggestions appear as the user types
aria-expanded state change is announced when the suggestion list appears
aria-controls links the input and suggestion list for assistive technology
aria-activedescendant tracks the highlighted item without moving DOM focus from the input
Arrow key navigation is the standard pattern for suggestion list traversal
Escape gives users a reliable way to abort the autocomplete
Live region suggestion count announcements orient screen reader users
Free text input is essential — forced selection breaks the experience for unusual input
responsiveGridPresets: Inline input with an absolutely positioned suggestion list below; full-width on mobile.

accessibilityRequirements: Apply role='tooltip' to the tooltip container element
Reference the tooltip from its trigger via aria-describedby
Show the tooltip on both hover AND keyboard focus — never hover-only
Dismiss the tooltip on Escape key or when focus/hover leaves the trigger
Do not put essential information only in a tooltip
Ensure tooltip text has sufficient contrast against its background
accessibilityRationale: role='tooltip' allows assistive technology to identify and announce supplementary information
aria-describedby associates the tooltip with its trigger so screen readers announce it on focus
Focus-triggered display ensures keyboard users receive the same hint as mouse hover users
Escape dismissal allows users to remove an obscuring tooltip
Essential information in tooltips-only is inaccessible to touch-only users with no hover state
Contrast requirements apply to tooltip text as they do to body content
responsiveGridPresets: Absolutely positioned relative to the trigger; auto-repositions to avoid viewport edges.
